newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Electricidad de Caracas sees rate hike soon.
newsitem.headline: Electricidad de Caracas sees rate hike soon.

text.p: Leading Venezuelan utility Electricidad de Caracas believes it will receive its long awaited rate rise soon, but bemoaned that the sector still wasn't governed by a clear regulatory framework.

"With yesterday's agreement on severance pay, Venezuelans will soon have more money in their pocket ... it opens the way for approval of the rate rise," said a high-placed source who asked not to be identified.

Venezuelan government, business and union leaders signed an historic severance pay agreement Monday which will see workers paid 25 percent of their accumulated severance pay over the next six months. The amount is expected to top 3.5 trillion bolivars ($7 billion), according to past Finance Ministry estimates.

Electricidad, which has long waged battle with the Ministry of Energy and Mines over delayed rate increases, is currently operating in a regulatory vacuum after an old system used to calculate increases was scrapped last year.
"Tariff increases are now meant to be based on the concept of 'an adequate return' in the context of 22 percent inflation for the year ... it's not clear what that means," said the source.
The increase has already been technically worked out by regulatory agency CREE, and only needs ministerial approval, the source said.
"If only the same thing happened to us as happened to CANTV," said the source. Last week, the government approved briefly delayed rate increases for telephone company CANTV.

Government sources told Reuters earlier in March that Electricidad de Caracas had asked for an average 40 percent rise based on an 85 percent increase for domestic users and 25 percent for commercial users, "but that was considered a lot."
Market analysts have expected an average increase of between 15 and 20 percent for the company.
